title: Outfit combinations
observableEvidence: Uses the multiplication counting principle to count the number of ways to combine one item from each of several independent groups.
prompt: A student has 4 different shirts and 3 different pairs of pants. If an outfit consists of one shirt and one pair of pants, how many different outfits are possible?
solutionMethod: Multiply the number of choices for the shirt by the number of choices for the pants, since each shirt can be paired with each pair of pants.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept with or without the word 'outfits'.

hintSteps.prompt: Think about how many pants choices go with just one particular shirt.
hintSteps.question: If you pick one shirt, how many outfits can you make with that one shirt?

hintSteps.prompt: Every shirt can be paired with the same number of pants choices.
hintSteps.question: How many shirts are there in total to repeat that same pairing for?

hintSteps.prompt: This is the same idea as a restaurant menu with 4 entrees and 3 side dishes, where each entree can be served with any side.
hintSteps.question: What is 4 times 3?

review.originalityStatement: Original scenario written for this repository, inspired only by the general Math Kangaroo skill type of multiplication-counting-principle reasoning; no problem reproduced from any contest archive.

accessibilityNotes: Present the shirt and pants counts in plain text; no diagram is required for this item.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A student has 4 different shirts and 3 different pairs of pants. Find how many different one-shirt-one-pants outfits are possible.
